subject: Re: Response tailstorm — Hosted API p95/p99 spike / Exec attention
messages:
From: ops@acme-fin.com
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Prod] Hosted API — sudden p99 spike, 503s and throughput loss

Hi team,

We started seeing a sharp deterioration in response times on your hosted API for our production tenant around 08:45 PDT today. Key observations:
- p95 up from ~220ms to ~1.1s; p99 approaching 6.4s on several routes.
- Error rate increased (5xx) — roughly 1.2% of requests in the last 30m, mostly 503s.
- Sustained throughput drop of ~20% for our chat endpoints (we're on model redwood-large-x).

Attached is a small latency digest (latency_digest_20270518.csv). Our SLOs are breached for the first time this quarter; leadership is asking for an explanation and ETA for mitigation.

Can you triage and propose mitigation steps? If this needs exec escalation, let us know — Jane (cc'd) is watching.

Thanks,
Sam (ops@acme-fin.com)
Acme Finance — Platform SRE
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acme-fin.com, Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Prod] Hosted API — sudden p99 spike, 503s and throughput loss

Sam / Jane —

Thanks for the heads up and the digest. We see matching alert noise in our platform. Immediate steps we're taking:
- Rishi is running a live kernel/profile capture on the cluster that served your traffic to check for GPU memory state and fragmentation.
- We'll provision a short-lived routing patch to move a portion of your traffic to a healthy pool (minimal config change) to reduce blast radius.
- Laura will coordinate a customer-facing note and confirm whether a short relief credit is appropriate once we have root cause.

I'll update within 30 minutes or sooner if we have a mitigation.

—Vivek
VP, Production Services
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acme-fin.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Prod] Hosted API — sudden p99 spike, 503s and throughput loss

Quick triage notes:
- Observed increased GPU free fragmentation on nodes that processed large-embedding and long-context chat requests. Active memory available but unusable due to slab fragmentation.
- Several nodes are hitting transient allocation failures and returning 503s while the runtime attempts slab compaction/eviction.
- I've pulled a heap snapshot from one affected worker (attached: gpu_heap_snapshot_20270519.bin).
- Short-term mitigation: draining affected nodes and routing traffic to a different pool reduces p99 on our canary by ~60%.

Action items:
1) Push routing patch (Vivek/infra) to shift 30% of Acme traffic to pool-b.
2) Schedule a rolling restart window for the affected node set to force memory defragmentation (low-risk; will be throttled).
3) Postmortem ticket for runtime engineering to investigate allocator behavior and slab compaction heuristics.

I will keep live logs streaming to the incident channel.

—Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acme-fin.com, Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-fin.com>

Sam / Jane —

We've pushed the routing patch and shifted ~35% of your production traffic to an unaffected pool. Early telemetry (10m) shows p99 improving from 6.4s -> ~2.0s on the routed subset; overall p99 for the tenant is trending down but not fully recovered.

Next steps:
- We'll perform a staggered rolling restart tonight (target: 23:00 PDT) for the affected worker set to reclaim fragmented memory.
- Rishi will continue analysis; runtime team on standby for a deeper allocator fix.
- Laura, please prepare a short status note for Acme leadership and include potential credit options.

Evelyn: asking you to join the customer call at 11:30 to align on SLAs and messaging.

—Vivek

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-fin.com>, ops@acme-fin.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:46:00 -0700
Subject: Incident summary and exec brief (Acme Finance)

Team / Jane —

Post-incident executive summary:
- Incident window: 2027-05-18T08:45:00-07:00 -> 2027-05-19T04:12:00-07:00 (primary impact).
- Root cause: GPU memory slab fragmentation in the inference runtime triggered by a confluence of long-context chat sessions and frequent large-embedding bursts. Fragmentation led to transient allocation failures and elevated 5xx rates.
- Mitigations performed: fast-routing to healthy pools, staggered rolling restarts of affected node set, and live heap captures for runtime engineering.
- Short-term customer impact: elevated p95/p99 and ~1.2% 5xx during the window; throughput reduced ~20% at peak.
- Remediation plan: runtime team will land allocator heuristic changes to avoid fragmentation under mixed workloads (ETA: 3 weeks), add proactive slab compaction job on low-util windows, and improve cluster-level routing to detect early fragmentation patterns (ETA: 2 weeks for detection rules).
- Customer remediation: Acme will receive a one-time service credit; Laura to confirm amount with finance.

Attached: final latency digest, heap snapshot, and the SLO exemption request we filed while the event was investigated.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
